answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, so repeated self-attestations do not create independent influence. A sybil cluster connected to honest nodes by few edges forms a sparse external cut with low conductance; spectral expansion and min-cut transitivity bounds constrain walk entry into that cluster and therefore its aggregate voting weight. Shared metadata—a mesa location, pigment tag, or coordinated signal—does not overcome the bottleneck.
